title: Fair Rules Are Not Always Fair Systems

quick.hook: Ambedkar asked why society was designed to deny dignity to some people.
quick.story: Ambedkar saw that unfair treatment was not only about one cruel person. It was built into rules, habits, and social structures.

bigIdea.title: Look beneath the surface of fairness
bigIdea.explanation: A society is not fair just because it has rules. It is fair when those rules protect everyone's dignity.

thinkingTool.name: Ask who benefits from the system
thinkingTool.instruction: When something is called normal or fair, ask who gains from it and who pays the hidden cost.

modernTest.scenario: Your school says everyone has equal opportunity, but some students can afford tutors, laptops, and quiet rooms while others cannot.
modernTest.question: What would Ambedkar ask first?

options.label: Who starts the race with hidden advantages?
options.explanation: This looks at structural fairness, not only individual effort.

options.label: Who studied the hardest?
options.explanation: Effort matters, but it does not erase unequal starting points.

modernTest.discussionNotes: Ambedkar would ask about the system, not only the exam rules on paper.

quick.reflectionPrompt: Identify one system in your life that looks fair on the surface but may not be fair underneath.

thoughtTension.counterView: But if everyone follows the same exam rules, is that not fairness?
thoughtTension.responsePrompt: Explain where you agree or disagree.

full.hook: Ambedkar did not just ask for a better life. He asked why society was designed to deny dignity to some people.
full.story: B. R. Ambedkar grew up in a society where caste decided how people were treated before they had a chance to prove who they were. He became a scholar, lawyer, and one of the chief architects of India's Constitution, but his deepest question was moral: can a society call itself fair if its rules protect dignity for some and humiliation for others?

bigIdea.title: Look beneath the surface of fairness
bigIdea.explanation: A society is not fair just because it has rules. It is fair only when those rules protect everyone's dignity.

thinkingTool.name: Ask who benefits from the system
thinkingTool.instruction: When something is called normal or fair, ask who gains from it and who pays the hidden cost.

modernTest.scenario: Your school says everyone has equal opportunity. Some students can afford tutors, laptops, quiet rooms, and private coaching. Others cannot.
modernTest.question: Is the competition still fair?

options.explanation: This recognizes that fairness is not always obvious.
